quote_text:
Yeah, I am to be honest. Scratching  my head a little bit. I don't think  
3-1 is a fair reflection of the  game at all. It's not often you  
play Rangers and you have more of the  ball, more passes, better chances,  
clearer chances, more shots – and we've  done all of that today, yet we've lost.
I suppose the story of the game for us is that  we weren’t clinical in those moments, and maybe  
a little bit of misfortune for one or two of the  goals as well, and that’s what’s decided the game.  
But yeah, so many positive things. I thought we  were very good. I thought we were excellent, took  
the game to them, went toe-to-toe with them, and I  don’t think 3-1 is a fair reflection of the game.
I thought we were excellent. I thought, you  know, there’s a risk to how we wanted to set  
up and play because they've got good players. If  your timing is not quite right on your press or  
you make the wrong decisions, then they have the  ability and technical quality to play through you,  
which they did a couple of times. But  we defended those moments really well,  
and off the back of that, when we won  the ball – which was numerous times – we  
then transitioned into the space they left  us, and we created lots of opportunities.
Elion and James and Shanks joining  up, Jo joining with the front two,  
we just didn’t take those opportunities. I  thought tactically, what we tried to do worked,  
but we were just relying on those moments going  our way, and unfortunately, they haven’t today.
Yeah, it is, yeah. And those are the things  that you need to go your way in these types  
of games. The first goal just obviously  hits Jimmy as he's recovering to the goal,  
and then the third goal, he’s actually  back there and doesn’t quite get enough  
on it to take it away from Dessers  and kick it out for a corner.
But even at 3-1, we've had  some big chances to go 3-2,  
and there was more than enough time left.  So yeah, I’m disappointed with the result,  
but not our performance today because I felt  we probably deserved more from the game.
Yeah, you could see Michael tiring in the second  half. He obviously started to stretch his calves,  
which is understandable. This is his first  start, and he's only three weeks into his  
time with us after having five or six weeks  off. I thought he was really good. I think  
he’s already shown in this short period of  time that when he gets fitter, stronger,  
and finds rhythm, he's going to  be a really good player for us.
He’ll help develop us in the way we want to  play, and it was a terrific header from the goal,  
from the corner, which is an added  bonus. Center-backs like him and  
Jimmy have become a real threat at set  pieces, which is an added bonus for us.
No, no, not at all. Not from  this type of performance. We can  
repeat this type of performance. Not many  teams have more of the ball than Rangers,  
home or away, and we've done that today.  We've played some really good football,  
created really good chances,  and we just didn’t take them.
It’s as simple as that. That’s why we’ve lost.  
But no, we’ve got seven games to the split,  and we want to be in the top six. So we go to  
St. Johnstone next week, and we’re going  to try and bounce back from this game.
No, I haven’t seen that back yet,  to be honest with you. There was a  
shout, but it was on the far side of the  penalty area, so I didn’t quite see it.  
We didn’t protect or counter-press our  attack well enough after that, though.
We should have stopped them from getting to  the edge of the box sooner, but I have to say,  
Adams put a terrific block in, and then  it’s just fallen straight into Cyriel  
Dessers’ path. It’s hit him and dropped for  him, and he’s very clinical in those moments.
Yeah, and if you don’t get the press right, it  does put more pressure on defenders. That’s why  
you recruit certain types of players to be able to  deal with those situations. If you look at all of  
our back four today, they have the mobility  to be able to cope in one-v-one situations.
If you're pressing forward, you're  going to expose yourself to big spaces,  
and in those moments, you need intelligent  players and players who can defend when they’re  
isolated in one-v-one situations.  I thought we did that well today.
They obviously showed their quality near  the end of the game when they were breaking  
into space. They’re very clinical. If  you look at the stats behind a lot of  
their performances this season, they’re the  best counter-attacking team in the league.
That doesn’t necessarily add up because  of the amount of possession they have,  
meaning they should be less of  a threat going the other way,  
but they play that little half-space position  really well, and they’re very dangerous on the  
break. When the pitch opens up, they've got good  quality players, and we felt that near the end.
But we also wanted to carry on going for the  game. Even at 3-1, we had big moments to go  
3-2. With more than enough time left, Butland  made some good saves, and we missed the target  
a few times. If we score and go 3-2, who knows?  We could have gotten something from the game.
Yeah, I spoke to Elion, and obviously, he’s  disappointed. He came off the pitch, and yeah,  
he’s frustrated. He said, ‘I should have  scored.’ But again, I’m not critical of him  
because he played that position perfectly, how we  wanted him to play. He got into the right areas.
Again, Butland produced a magnificent save, low  down, to tip it around the post, and then that  
other one where it hit his arm and deflected  past the goal – you just need one of those to  
go through. It just didn’t quite happen for him  today. He could have easily had one or two goals.
Yeah, he’s okay. He’s been back on the  pitch running, but he wasn’t quite right,  
so we weren’t going to risk him  today. His health is more important,  
and we obviously prioritize that. But  hopefully this week, since he’s been  
back out doing some running, we can progress  that, and he’ll be available for next week.
title: Neil Critchley Post Match Press Conference | Hearts 1-3 Rangers
